alignments.note: אוֹ takes the written *Or*.

The relative אֲשֶׁר is what the ASV's conditional *if* is written for; a present subordinating morpheme takes the word before a supplied reading does (rules 46, 55), and counting the clause's subordinators against the ASV's leaves neither side in surplus.
נֶפֶשׁ → *any one*; the supplied quantifying determiner joins the nominal under rule 15.
Finite verb.
The ASV promotes the object of בְּ to a bare direct object, leaving the preposition nothing (rule 40).
כֹּל standing on the noun is itself what the ASV's *any* renders (rule 15).
Attributive adjective.
Noun.
The four אוֹ of the verse are counted against the ASV's *Or ... whether ... or ... or*; this one takes *whether* (rule 14).

Corrected from the accepted reading, which gave this בְּ the copula and dummy subject *it be* under rule 49. Rule 49's closing sentence says every one of its sentences governs a phrase for which the ASV has written an English preposition, and here it writes none; nor is the relation written inside the following word, so the fusion branch is not reached either. The ASV spends no word on what this preposition contributes, so it is unrepresented under rule 40, exactly as the verse's three other בְּ are.

Construct noun with the supplied *the* (rule 29); the construction-supplied copula and its dummy subject join the predicate this clause is recast around, exactly as rule 20 gives the supplied *it was* of *that it was good* to the unit headed on טוֹב. Competing reading: put *it be* on the preposition בְ under rule 49, which is the reading corrected here.
Rectum takes the relational *of*; the indefinite article joins the noun (rules 15, 19). Discontinuous around the adjective.
Attributive adjective.
Second אוֹ takes *or*.
The ASV writes no preposition and no second copula for this member (rule 40).
Construct noun with supplied *the* (rule 29).
Rectum takes *of*; discontinuous around the adjective.
Attributive adjective.
Third אוֹ takes *or*.
No English word for this preposition (rule 40).
Construct noun with supplied *the*.
Rectum takes *of*; *creeping things* heads on *creeping*, which carries the lexeme, since *things* alone is any things (rule 31). Discontinuous around the adjective.
Attributive adjective.
Waw takes *and*.
Niphal verb with subject pronoun and copula, headed on the lexical participle.
Preposition.
Suffix takes the object pronoun.
Waw takes *and*.
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own *he* (rule 20).
Predicate adjective carries the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
Apodosis waw takes *then* (rule 14).
Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliaries, headed on the complement *guilty* (rule 44).

review_notes: Corrected: the first בְּ (s010) had been given *it be* under rule 49. Rule 49 governs only a phrase for which the ASV has written an English preposition, and none is written here, so the preposition is unrepresented under rule 40 and the copula with its dummy subject joins the predicate nominal under rule 20. All four בְּ of the verse are now read alike.
The four אוֹ are counted against the ASV's *Or ... whether ... or ... or*, one English connective per morpheme, so rule 14's correlative-pair clause is not reached.
אֲשֶׁר takes the conditional *if*: a subordinating morpheme stands in the clause, so rule 55's added case does not apply.
